subject: No-improve commitment for MedNova pilot — SOW & subprocessor routing
messages:
From: Simon Hargreaves <simon.h@mednova.co.uk>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@mednova.co.uk
Date: 2026-05-20T09:10:00-04:00
Subject: Clarify pilot data use — model improvement & subprocessors

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick onboarding work so far. Before we kick off the pilot (scope: 4-week clinical triage integration), LegalOps asked me to confirm a couple of privacy/contract items so we can move procurement and get signatures:

1) Training/no-improve: Can you confirm that MedNova pilot data (customer-provided prompts and patient-facing responses) will not be used to improve Redwood models or any third-party models? We need language we can put in our SOW/DPA that explicitly excludes the pilot data from model improvement.

2) Prompt/response ownership: Our team needs confirmation that outputs generated during the pilot are exclusively controlled/owned by MedNova for the duration of the engagement and for export purposes.

3) Subprocessor scope & geo routing: Please provide the current subprocessor inventory you expect to process pilot requests and confirm whether any subprocessors will see raw interaction data outside the UK/EU. If so, we need onshore routing options (EU-only) or controls we can rely on.

4) Evidence for audit: LegalOps would like SOC2 + a short operational description for how you enforce the no-training commitment (e.g., runtime toggles, KV cache handling, short-term retention, KMS residency).

If you can share a short SOW template or proposed DPA redlines that include the no-improve commitment and subprocessor routing, LegalOps will review and aim to respond this week. We may have a few redlines but want to get the contract moving.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a 30-min call if easier.

Best,
Simon
Head of Security Operations
MedNova

[Note: added procurement@mednova.co.uk per contracting request]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Hargreaves <simon.h@mednova.co.uk>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T11:25:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify pilot data use — model improvement & subprocessors

Simon —

Thanks for outlining the asks. Short answers up front: yes, we can commit the pilot dataset to a no-model-improve posture, and we can produce an SOW + DPA redline that codifies that commitment and the output ownership model. We can also provide the current subprocessor inventory and an EU-only routing option for MedNova traffic.

What I will do next:
- Attach an initial SOW draft that includes a clear "No Model Improvement / No Adaptive Training" clause and an output ownership paragraph for pilot outputs (attached: redwood_no_train_sow_v1.docx).
- Attach our proposed DPA redlines that highlight the subprocessor routing and residency options (will attach DPA redlines once legal finalizes; preliminary notes below).
- Share the subprocessor inventory CSV and a short ops note describing how we implement runtime exclusion and short-term retention.

Can you confirm the following to help us tailor the SOW:
- Will MedNova require KMS keys onshore (customer-managed) or is Redwood-managed EU KMS acceptable?
- Any minimum retention windows for logs or transcripts you need for clinical QA (e.g., 30/90 days)?

I'll loop in Kimberly to confirm the contract language and David to confirm ops implementation. If MedNova prefers, I can schedule a 30-minute legal+ops sync on Wednesday.

Thanks —
Priyom
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_no_train_sow_v1.docx (draft SOW)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T09:00:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify pilot data use — model improvement & subprocessors (internal)

Priyom / David / Marissa —

Quick internal read on the SOW draft and MedNova asks. High-level edits we should make before sending externally:

1) Contract language (SOW + DPA redline):
   - "No Model Improvement" clause: explicit "Redwood shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning model, including third-party models, during the term of the pilot and for 12 months after unless Customer provides written consent."
   - "Output Ownership": Customer retains all rights to prompts and generated outputs for the pilot; Redwood grants a limited license to operate the service for the sole purpose of providing the contracted service.
   - Add narrow "staging/telemetry" carveouts only for operational diagnostics, with TTL <= 30 days and anonymization where possible.

2) Subprocessors & geo-fencing:
   - Provide an explicit subprocessor inventory (current + proposed) and commit to EU-only routing for MedNova requests. If any subprocessor must process outside EU, require prior written notice and offer onshore alternative or customer-managed KMS.
   - Add an audit clause allowing MedNova to request subprocessor attestations (SOC2/ISO) and a one-time evidence package.

3) Technical controls:
   - Runtime toggle (no-train flag) documented in SOW and enforced at the request router level.
   - KV/prefix cache: session keys isolated and expired within 30 days for pilot.
   - Logging: redact PHI in logs by default; logs retained for 30 days unless a retention exception is requested via legal.

4) Operational timeline & ask list to send to MedNova:
   - Subprocessor CSV (attach)
   - Draft DPA redlines (we will produce PDF with tracked changes)
   - Short ops note describing runtime toggle and KMS residency options

I suggest we send the SOW + subprocessor CSV now and the DPA redlines (with highlighted clauses) by Monday morning. David — can ops confirm EU-only routing and TTL enforcement by EOD tomorrow? Marissa — please prep the DPA redline covering the audit/evidence language.

-Kimberly
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify pilot data use — model improvement & subprocessors

Simon / LegalOps team —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled materials together. Short summary of commitments for the pilot and next steps:

- No-model-improvement: Redwood will enforce a runtime "no-train" posture for the MedNova pilot. We will include the following language in the SOW and DPA redline: "Redwood will not use Customer Data from the MedNova pilot to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning model (Redwood or third party) during the term of the pilot and for 12 months thereafter without Customer's prior written consent."

- Output ownership: Outputs (prompts and generated responses) are retained by MedNova for export and use. Redwood's use of those outputs is limited to operating the service under the contract.

- Subprocessor routing & inventory: Attached is the current subprocessor inventory (subprocessor_inventory_2026.csv). Per our operations team, we can route MedNova traffic to EU-only endpoints and use EU-keyed KMS. If any subprocessor change requires processing outside the EU, Redwood will provide prior notice and an onshore alternative where feasible.

- Operational evidence: Attached are the SOW draft (redwood_no_train_sow_v1.docx) and our DPA redlines (DPA_mednova_redlines_v2.pdf). The DPA redlines include the audit clause (one-time evidence package: SOC2 + subprocessor attestations). For runtime enforcement, we implement a no-train flag at the router layer, KV/session TTLs settable per-customer (default 30 days for the pilot), and redaction-first logging for PHI.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached SOW and DPA redlines and provide any specific redlines you expect by EOD Friday.
2) If the language looks good, LegalOps can accept the DocuSign envelope at: https://docusign.com/embedded-sign/abc123.
3) Operations onboarding call — propose Tue 2026-05-28 10:00 BST / 05:00 EDT to run through routing and KMS options. Let me know if that works.

If you want a one-time operational walkthrough before signature, I can include David on the call to demonstrate routing and TTL enforcement.

Cheers,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
